name: Strand
text: The Strand (commonly referred to with a leading "The", but formally without) is a major street in the City of Westminster, Central London. The street, which is part of London's West End theatreland, runs just over 3⁄4 mile (1.2 km) from Trafalgar Square eastwards to Temple Bar, where it becomes Fleet Street in the City of London, and is part of the A4, a main road running west from central London. The road's name comes from the Old English strond, meaning the beach or edge of a river, as it historically ran alongside the north bank of the River Thames.

depictions.name: The Strand
depictions.text: Strand, London The Strand is a bustling borough of London that served as the city's principal shopping area during the Industrial Revolution, and featured a sizeable public park. Thieves usually operated in this area due to the abundance of unaware victims. The borough were overseen by Templar Victor Lynch; to take over The Strand, Jacob and Evie Frye had to take down several threats.
